facts.claim: "In My Room" by Medium Build was released as a single on December 8, 2023. It runs about 2:42, and its P-line says it is under exclusive license to Island Records.
Deezer lists the composers as Nicholas Carpenter, Carrie K and Jake LiBassi. Jake LiBassi is the 'Laiko' named in other credit listings.
Credit aggregator listings name Carrie K and Laiko as producers of the track, and Carrie K, Laiko and Medium Build as writers.
Hashtag Magazine says the song is about Nick Carpenter's upbringing and his bedroom as a place of solace growing up. The music video shows his own room.
Carpenter told the Tennessean the song came from a writing prompt about his childhood room. He described himself as a passive kid whose parents were chaotic church people.
The song is track 2 on Medium Build's 2024 album Country (slowplay/Island, April 5, 2024). It was one of four tracks released before the album.
Country was recorded on Nashville's Music Row with creative partner Laiko.
Atwood Magazine reports that Carpenter and LiBassi recorded the core of Country over about a week in a publishing studio off Music Row. They called in friends to play various parts.
Medium Build is the project of singer-songwriter Nick Carpenter. It began in 2015 with the song 'Stupider', and he developed it after living in Alaska in his twenties.
Carpenter signed to slowplay/Island Records in 2023. AllMusic lists 'In My Room' among the buzzy singles from that period, alongside 'Rage' and 'Say Hi' and the EP Health (2023).

research.lineage: Medium Build's music sits in a folk-rock and indie-folk singer-songwriter tradition with country, Americana and '80s new wave influences. Carpenter built it from a DIY Anchorage scene and a Nashville base.

draft:
The detail that sets everything up comes early: when Dad gets home from an eleven-hour shift, the kid loses the TV. Nobody is cruel in **"In My Room."** Mom is stressed trying to make sure everyone eats, big brother is numbing out on the PlayStation, and the house is too full of tired people for a quiet kid to take up space. So he goes to his room.

Nick Carpenter, who records as Medium Build, told the Tennessean the song grew out of a writing prompt about his childhood bedroom. He described himself back then as a passive kid whose parents were chaotic church people. The song doesn't argue with that house. It just lists what happens behind the door, and the list is funny, embarrassing and honest at once: a Simpsons poster, a Weird Al tape, learning guitar, "Makin' action figures kiss." That line is a child rehearsing tenderness with the only company that won't laugh at him. The second verse turns the room outward. There's a friend, a bus ride the moms arranged, melted cheese on chips, a Matrix quote deployed to seem interesting. Then comes the nervous request to sleep over and talk about life all night, and you can hear how much rides on a yes.

The sound keeps all of this close. Fingerpicked acoustic guitar rolls in arpeggios over a bass that mostly holds the root. The drums settle in on kick, snare and hi-hat before moving to the ride. The tempo is medium and the groove relaxed with a slight swing. The mix is clean, with a little reverb on a single voice and no harmonies. Carpenter sings smooth and calm, never pleading, which suits a kid who learned not to make noise. It sits in the indie-folk singer-songwriter lane he built between Anchorage's DIY scene and Nashville. He wrote it with Carrie K and Jake LiBassi, also known as Laiko, who produced it, and it became track two on the album Country, recorded on Music Row.

Then the last verse does something quietly crushing. Right after "I am sacred, I am safe, I am free," the song stops saying "I." It describes "a kid" from the outside: wearing his brother's clothes, hating how he looks, bad at saying no, working hard so none of it shows. The grown man can only look at that boy from across the room. The first chorus wished for enough money to never feel lonely at home. The answer is softer and sadder: "And sometimes he's alone when he's at home."

You come away remembering whatever room you hid in, and finally hearing what the kid inside it couldn't say.
